title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
A platform that attracts 13 million monthly visitors deployed a system that allows users to create and distribute deepfake pornographic videos by superimposing the faces of real people, including celebrities, politicians, and members of the royal family, onto adult film footage. The platform allegedly incentivized this content by paying uploaders more for videos with higher viewership and advising them to remain anonymous. No automated detection or human review caught this deployment as harmful before victims discovered they were featured.

The failure was one of permitting a generative capability to run without safeguards against non-consensual sexual imagery. The system created a product that violates the dignity and autonomy of people whose likenesses were used without their knowledge or consent. It would have taken either refusing the capability altogether, implementing detection to catch non-consensual deepfakes before publication, or maintaining human review of uploaded content to prevent this harm.

It is not established whether the platform's operators intended to facilitate abuse or were indifferent to the consequences of their design choices.

summary:
Several female Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after appearing in manipulated pornographic videos on an online platform that attracts 13 million monthly visitors. The videos feature various public figures including entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government ministers, mayors, and members of the Dutch royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos appalling and encouraged victims to report them to authorities. Managers and representatives of affected individuals confirmed to the news service that some have filed complaints or are exploring legal options.

These deepfake pornography videos work by placing a celebrity's face onto adult film footage. The platform allegedly advises uploaders to remain anonymous and pays them more for videos that receive higher viewership. Legal experts warn that without government intervention, more fake pornography featuring celebrities will emerge. Deepfake material falls under revenge pornography laws and is punishable by law. Victims have several options including filing reports with prosecutors who can attempt to shut down the website, launching group lawsuits, filing complaints with data protection authorities, or contacting hosting companies.
